# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 4

**1** After fifteen days, during which I had fasted and earnestly sought the Lord, the meaning of the writing was revealed to me. It read as follows: **2** "Your offspring have sinned against God, Hermas, and they have blasphemed the Lord, and have betrayed their parents through great wickedness, and have been called betrayers of their parents. And though they betrayed them, they gained nothing by it — they only heaped more transgressions upon their sins. **3** And riotous living and wanton wickedness were added on top, so that the full measure of your children's transgressions has been filled up. **4** But you know that God is merciful, and he will heal the sins of your household, if you repent with your whole household and humble yourselves before the Lord and serve him with pure hearts — then he will heal all your former sins." **5** "Do not be disheartened over your household, but continue to admonish them. For just as a goldsmith refines his work through fire, so also God refines those who are his own — especially those who truly belong to him." There the message ended.

---

### Council Notes

The revelation of the heavenly book's content (which Hermas has been carrying for fifteen days without understanding) focuses entirely on the domestic situation: the children's sins, their betrayal, and the path of corporate household repentance.

The repeated emphasis on household repentance (chs. 2, 5, 12) reflects the social reality of early Christianity as a house-church movement, where the faith was transmitted through family units. The head of household bore spiritual responsibility for all.

The goldsmith simile (v. 5) echoes the blacksmith image of ch. 2 — Hermas favors craft-workshop metaphors for moral formation.
